prompt:
An electric train of mass 1.8 x 10^5 kg travels along a straight horizontal track.
(a) At a steady cruising speed of 30 m s^-1, the train motors deliver a total mechanical power of 1.08 MW. Calculate the total resistive force opposing the train. [1]
(b) The driver selects maximum motor power of 1.62 MW while the train is still travelling at 30 m s^-1. Assuming the resistive force remains unchanged at this instant:
(i) calculate the new total forward tractive force developed by the wheels [1]
(ii) calculate the resultant forward force acting on the train [1]
(iii) calculate the initial acceleration of the train [1]

mark_scheme.criterion: (a) Calculates resistive force: F_resist = P / v = (1.08 * 10^6) / 30 = 36 000 N (or 36 kN).
(b)(i) Calculates new tractive force: F_new = (1.62 * 10^6) / 30 = 54 000 N (or 54 kN).
(b)(ii) Calculates resultant force: F_res = 54 000 - 36 000 = 18 000 N (or 18 kN).
(b)(iii) Calculates acceleration: a = F_res / m = 18 000 / (1.8 * 10^5) = 0.10 m s^-2.

hints: In (a), rearrange P = Fv to find force.
In (b)(i), use new power 1.62 MW at 30 m s^-1.
In (b)(ii), subtract resistive force from the new tractive force.
In (b)(iii), apply Newton's second law a = F_res / m.
teacher_walkthrough: Part (a): Cruising speed means equilibrium: F_resist = P / v = 1 080 000 / 30 = 36 kN.
Part (b)(ii): Resultant force = 54 kN - 36 kN = 18 kN.
